notes.detailedSummary: Complete all-support proof of primaryness, grading, raw C/D identity, full-degree convergence and continuity criterion, rational attainment iff canonical finite generation, gauges, conditional conductor descent and geometric reduced-curve clipping. No general positivity of a raw supremum or FG density.
notes.text:
Relative only to the ENTIRE qualified G331, let R be excellent local, replace it by Rred, and fix a proper primary ideal a. Its positive-dimensional section X=V_a(R) includes EVERY support; dimension zero has the unique empty envelope. Write C for the continuous independently geometric class and D for its actual decreasing-net completion. G331 identifies these with the corresponding ideal classes, after defining positivity by actual negative effective real Cartier presentations and every contracted-curve degree test on directed actual primary blowups. This comparison, rational profile density, finite maxima, and full-fibre positive descent are used with every source/scope qualification. No envelope theorem is imported.

For finite continuous signed f define A_0=R and A_m={g: v(g)+m f(v)>=0 for ALL v in X}. If c=max(0,-min f), then a^N is contained in A_m for every positive N>=mc. Ultrametric addition and nonnegative ring values make A_m an ideal. If f is negative somewhere no unit satisfies the defining inequality, so every positive-degree A_m is proper primary. Otherwise A_m=R. Multiplication gives A_m A_n subset A_(m+n). Every A_m is integrally closed: in a monic ideal-integrality equation, v(g)<v(A_m) would make the leading term uniquely least of finite value. Infinite v(g) causes no exception. The finite continuous profile h_m=-v(A_m)/m lies below f and is geometrically positive: -E_(A_m)/m is actual negative effective Cartier and relatively ample on its actual primary blowup. Unit profiles are zero.

Define the RAW function p(f)=sup{u in D:u<=f}, without asserting positivity of this supremum. It equals the supremum over C and sup_m h_m. Indeed a rational competitor -v(I)/r<=f has I subset A_r. A C competitor is uniformly approximated by rational profiles; shift an approximant down by a small rational a-constant, realized by ideal multiplication and a common denominator, to obtain rational competitors arbitrarily close from below. For u=inf_i g_i<=f in an ACTUAL decreasing C-net, the open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X and are directed by inclusion. One index works everywhere. Then g_i-epsilon is a C competitor and u<=sup_m h_m+epsilon. Let epsilon decrease to zero. This handles bottom and partial poles without continuity of u.

Set M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(1<=r<=N)h_r in C. For m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, grading gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m>=h_r-rM_1/m; hence H_N-NM_1/m<=h_m<=p. Therefore the FULL h_m sequence converges pointwise to the finite nonpositive lower-semicontinuous p. Moreover p is continuous iff H_N converges uniformly iff h_m converges uniformly. If p is continuous, the increasing strict-error open sets for H_N cover compact X, proving uniform convergence; the residue bound transfers it to h_m. Conversely a uniform limit lies in closed C and equals p. In that case p is the greatest D minorant, with actual geometric positivity. Pointwise convergence alone supplies no regularity.

The raw map is sup-norm 1-Lipschitz. If f<=g+epsilon, subtract the fixed negative primary constant epsilon from a D competitor below f to obtain a D competitor below g. Supremizing and reversing f,g proves the bound. Thus uniform density of a specified class of obstacles with C envelopes would prove CE for its uniform closure; no general such finite-generation density is asserted.

For this FIXED obstacle, its canonical algebra A=direct-sum A_m t^m is finitely generated iff p is a rational unit-or-primary profile iff a finite maximum of canonical profiles attains p. To prove the forward direction, take homogeneous generators g_i t^(d_i), let L be divisible by all d_i and D_0=max d_i, and put J=(g_i^(L/d_i)). At each support some generator has finite value because A_1 contains a primary power. Degree-m expressions have value at least m min_i v(g_i)/d_i, while pure powers belong to A_L. Consequently p=h_L=-v(J)/L. A generator attaining the minimum also shows p=max_(r<=D_0)h_r. The radical of J contains A_1, so J is primary in the proper case. The residue bound yields 0<=p-h_m<=D_0 M_1/m uniformly on ALL supports.

Conversely suppose p=-v(J)/q with J primary and q positive integral. Since h_m<=p<=f, every g in A_m satisfies v(g)>=(m/q)v(J). The reverse implication follows from p<=f. Thus A_m={g:g^q in integral-closure(J^m)}. The equality uses the centred rank-one DVR criterion on every minimal-component domain quotient and the all-minimal-component criterion, precisely SH6.8.3--4 and 1.1.5. Every minimal component has positive dimension: otherwise the maximal ideal is minimal and the local reduction has dimension zero. Each centred DVR normalizes into X. Monic equations prove the reverse inequalities on every other support too. These complete immediate source units were freshly read, with formula bars checked in the actual PDF pixels; deeper valuation-domination foundations are named conventional background.

Let B=R[Jt^q]. A primary ideal contains a regular element by finite prime avoidance, so B is reduced excellent and has total quotient product K_j(t^q). Its finite extension product K_j(t) may be inseparable. Excellent/Nagata finite normalization makes the integral closure finite over B. An equation for g^q over J^m, multiplied by t^(mq) powers, makes g^q t^(mq) integral over B; the qth-power equation then makes gt^m integral. Hence A is a B-submodule of that finite normalization and is finite by Noetherianity. The unit case gives R[t]. A finite maximum of rational profiles is rational via sums of powered ideals. No arbitrary section algebra is assumed finitely generated.

For an integral signed exceptional Cartier obstacle f_D on an actual primary model over normal R, let Y be its finite normalization. The canonical rational trivialization gives A_m=H^0(Y,O(mD)) intersect R. All-boundary tests at exceptional height-one orders imply the section inequalities there; at other height-one primes g is regular and D vanishes. Normal height-one intersection gives section membership. Conversely pull the section to the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) for each support p. Properness gives its centre, and the generic point is outside the exceptional fibre. The invertible lattice has nonzero generic trivialization; if b generates it, v(g)>=v(b)=-m f_D(v). This is the defining inequality on every support, with infinite g values automatic. No original fraction field is mapped through p. This computation supplies no general finite-generation theorem.

For another primary b put d(v)=v(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v), transporting f by f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). The defining inequalities divide by d. ALL A_m and their algebra are literally unchanged; h_m and p divide by d, with the exact three-gauge cocycle. Uniform constants divide by min d>0. Finite normalization S gives A_m^R=A_m^S intersect R by surjective restriction. If a source envelope exists and is constant on EVERY fibre, G331 descends it positively; it dominates all pulled-back downstairs competitors, so is the downstairs envelope. Obstacle compatibility alone is insufficient, including on infinite-conductor quotient fibres. A decreasing family of continuous obstacles with C envelopes H_i has the actual D envelope inf_i H_i of its infimum: it is a minorant and every competitor lies below each H_i.

On every excellent reduced curve, normalization centres are DVRs and a regular conductor element has finite branch order. Thus boundary fibres are singletons. Actual real Cartier slopes on each DVR have no contracted-curve conditions and give every finite nonpositive coordinate. Semilocal gluing and G331 positive descent give C equal to the finite nonpositive orthant; decreasing coordinate truncations give the extended orthant D. Consequently the geometric envelope is min(f,0), matching the ideal envelope. This does not identify the valuative class with literal multibranch classical/CLD logarithmic radial extensions: the mixed-zero obstruction remains. Nilpotents are invisible and dimension-zero reduction has empty boundary. On a DVR the irrational obstacle -alpha has continuous real Cartier envelope, but A_m=(x^ceil(m alpha)) is not finitely generated: finite homogeneous generators would force a rational minimum order/degree ratio equal to alpha. Thus non-finite-generation is not a CE counterexample.

notes.text:
This note reconstructs the whole410 smooth and finite-quotient proofs, using only qualified G331, earlier own n1, and the exact BFJ published applications. The smooth source S is the local ring at a smooth affine CLOSED point over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension at least two. DVR and empty cases are n1. No smooth hypothesis is enlarged in applying BFJ.

In the maximal-ideal gauge take a finite continuous model obstacle F=F composed with r_pi0 and M=max(0,-min F). Signed primary ideal combinations are such model functions after common smooth principalization and are uniformly dense, by BFJ1.14--1.15. The weak coefficient envelope W of nef divisors below Z(F) is finite nef: replace competitors by maxima with the nef barrier -M, form their directed coefficientwise supremum, and use weak closedness. Thus -M<=W<=0. BFJ3.11 gives its function H with substantive continuity on every CLOSED simplex, extended by H(v)=inf_pi H(r_pi v). Divisorial density gives H<=F on each simplex; for refinements of pi0, F(r_pi v)=F(v), proving H<=F on every support. Also H>=-M. G331's exact BFJ comparison makes every nonbottom D competitor have nef coefficients below W and therefore full all-retraction extension below H. Thus H is the raw greatest D minorant; weak-topology continuity remains to prove.

Put B_m=L-infinity(mW)=L-infinity(mZ(F)) in the completion (BFJ3.15--3.17). These contain a positive primary power mhat^N for N>=mM. They contract exactly to n1's A_m. For the decisive converse from coefficient tests to ALL supports, let g pass those tests and consider the primary-or-unit ideal (g)+mhat^N. Its divisorial log-profile max(log|g|,-N)<=mF. Closed-simplex continuity and the cofinal refinements of pi0 extend the inequality to every semivaluation. Since v(g)>=v((g)+mhat^N), g satisfies the canonical inequality everywhere. The reverse implication is divisorial restriction. G331 completion homeomorphism and exact primary contraction then identify the ideals in S. Infinite values cause no exception.

If W=0, divisorial density gives F>=0 and all envelopes/profiles are zero. Otherwise BFJ3.14 gives H strictly negative. Thinness A is bounded ONLY on the fixed compact complex, and H is continuous there, so choose C>0 with A<=-CW there. The ENTIRE immediate proof of BFJ3.18, including3.22, gives W_t<=W<=(1-C/t)W_(t-C), where W_t=Z(L-infinity(tW))/t and t>C. This applies to real t: its first inequality has no C, and the proof's thinness step for (ii), followed by (i) applied to tW, proves (iii) for any real t>C. Hence t=m+C yields (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W. Extending coefficient inequalities through closed simplices and all retraction infima gives 0<=H-h_m<=CM/m on EVERY semivaluation. Uniform primary approximation proves H belongs to continuous geometric C. No finite generation is needed.

For arbitrary finite continuous signed F, approximate uniformly by signed primary model functions. Their C envelopes are uniformly Cauchy by n1's raw Lipschitz bound, and their limit is p(F). Closedness of C proves CE for every continuous signed obstacle at the exact published smooth hypotheses. Other primary gauges divide profiles and errors by their bounded positive denominator; canonical ideals are unchanged. G331 transports completion at these hypotheses without asserting an equivalence of model categories. All complete immediately applied BFJ units, including its setting, retractions, closed-simplex continuity, multiplier auxiliaries, and entire3.18 proof, were freshly physically read. Hironaka smooth characteristic-zero principalization, ordinary multiplier subadditivity, thinness computations and smooth Izumi are named deeper foundations, not recursively reproved.

Now let a finite faithful group G act by local automorphisms on such S, with R=S^G excellent Noetherian and S finite. R is normal: an invariant fraction integral over R is integral over normal S and lies in S^G. For K=Frac(R), L=Frac(S), clearing an invariant fraction's denominator by its orbit product gives L^G=K. The needed fixed-field theorem has a direct proof. Distinct automorphisms are L-linearly independent as functions: evaluating a shortest relation at ax and subtracting sigma_j(a) times its value at x gives a shorter nonzero relation if two automorphisms differ on a. Thus evaluation columns span L^d, d=|G|. Choose x_j giving an invertible evaluation matrix. Solving sigma_i(x)=sum_j c_j sigma_i(x_j) and applying any automorphism permutes rows, forcing c_j in K. The same matrix proves the x_j K-independent, hence [L:K]=d. Orbit polynomials are separable with invariant coefficients and split in L, so L/K is Galois with group G. S is its integral closure of R.

Fix primary a in R and b=aS. G331 gives continuous surjective rho:V_b(S)->V_a(R), retaining ALL supports. Its full normal-target coefficient trace gives mu_v=sum_(sigma in G)delta_(w composed with sigma) with SUPPORT(mu_v)=the ENTIRE restriction fibre. Hence every fibre is a full group orbit, including nonminimal supports. This uses the grant's valued QUOTIENT-field coefficient identity after killing supports, not fraction-field extension through a nonzero support.

For f downstairs, F=f composed with rho has a continuous geometric source envelope H_S by the smooth result. Uniqueness makes H_S invariant, hence constant on every fibre. G331 positive continuous descent gives H_R in C_R. Surjectivity gives H_R<=f, and any D_R competitor pulls back below H_S, hence is below H_R. Thus rho^*P_R(f)=P_S(F) and EVERY continuous signed obstacle has a C/D envelope on this finite smooth quotient.

Explicit positive approximants are coefficient norm ideals. B_m=A_m^S(F) is G-stable. Choose finite R-module generators s_i and let J_m be the coefficients of product_sigma(sum_i T_i sigma(s_i)). These coefficients lie in K and are integral over normal R, hence lie in R. G331 proves generator independence, primary-power containment, and on ALL supports v(J_m)=sum_sigma(w composed with sigma)(B_m)=d w(B_m). Thus kappa_m=-v(J_m)/(dm) pulls back exactly to h_m^S. J_m is unit or proper primary, and kappa_m is an actual negative effective nef Cartier profile below f. The sequence converges uniformly by source CE and n1. Also A_m^R=B_m intersect R; this does not imply finite generation.

For a signed REAL exceptional Cartier obstacle on an actual primary model of R, G331's fixed-primary section formula expresses it as a finite signed primary-ideal combination. After source principalization it is a model obstacle. Let e=CM/min_(nu in V_mS)nu(b)>0, allowing e=0 in the zero case. Then 0<=P_R-kappa_m<=e/m. Since J_m subset A_(dm)^R, h_(dm)^R>=kappa_m. For k>=2d, set m=floor(k/d), r=dm. Grading with (A_1^R)^(k-r) gives h_k^R>=h_r^R-dM_1^R/k. Therefore 0<=P_R-h_k^R<=e/floor(k/d)+dM_1^R/k<=(2de+dM_1^R)/k uniformly on EVERY support. This is fixed-obstacle regularity without canonical finite generation.

The actual nonisolated normal quotient example is S=k[x,y,z_1,...,z_r] at the origin, r>=1, with involution (-x,-y,z). Its invariant ring is R=k[a,b,c,z]/(ac-b^2) at the origin, a=x^2,b=xy,c=y^2. Reduced monomials give exactly this relation; orbit denominator products verify localization, and x,y satisfy monic quadratics, giving finiteness. Normality follows as above; excellence is finite-type. Dimension is r+2 and the singular locus (a,b,c) has dimension r: away from it a derivative is a unit, and along it embedding dimension exceeds local dimension by one. This finite cover is not normalization of already normal R.

For r=1, I=(a+b,b+c,z)+m^2, J=(a,c,z^2)+m^3, and f=v(I)-5/4+sin(v(J))/100 is finite continuous signed on every support. The injective substitution x=r0,y=r0(h-1) and weights (r0,h,z)=(1,1,6) gives normalized m value1, v(I)=3/2, v(J)=1. Monomial weights (x,y,z)=(1,1,6) have identical a,b,c,z values but v(I)=1 and v(J)=1. The two obstacle values are respectively 1/4+sin(1)/100 and -1/4+sin(1)/100. Thus cancellation changes the obstacle. CE is established for it, without a closed formula or finite-generation assertion. All gauge, nilpotent, curve and radial distinctions in n1 remain; products, energy and full finite-map operators are separate.

No literal mathematical flaw was found in the four current whole410 proofs at their explicit scopes. The real-parameter step above is justified from the complete published proof instead of inferred solely from the notation k. notes.summary: New exact separable coefficient-field descent gives all continuous envelopes on finite smooth quotients over any characteristic-zero field.
notes.detailedSummary: For geometrically integral/normal rational-point finite-type local domains, proves full profinite fibre orbits, trace-dual invariant ideal descent, EVERY-degree canonical base extension, raw envelope commutation, continuity/error/FG equivalences and invariant C descent. Applies BFJ only after algebraic closure; actual normal nonisolated quotients over Q included. General excellent/mixed scope remains open.
notes.text:
NEW algebraic-field descent, proved independently. Let k be any field, let (R,m) be a positive-dimensional normal domain essentially of finite type over k with residue field EXACTLY k, and assume geometric integrality and geometric normality. Fix primary a. Let k^s be a separable closure and put R_s=R tensor_k k^s. It is the local ring at the corresponding rational point: for every finite Galois E/k, R_E=R tensor_k E is finite free and has a unique maximal ideal, since R_E/mR_E=E and every maximal ideal in a finite integral algebra lies over m. The directed union is local, and is the corresponding finite-type localized k^s algebra, hence Noetherian excellent normal. Geometric hypotheses are explicit; no assertion about arbitrary excellent germs or completions is made. All semivaluation supports are retained.

Write X_E=V_(aR_E)(R_E), X_s=V_(aR_s)(R_s), and Gamma=Gal(k^s/k). G331 supplies surjective restriction at every finite stage. There is an actual homeomorphism X_s=lim_E X_E: a compatible tuple defines a semivaluation on the union, satisfies the axioms and a-normalization there, and conversely every semivaluation restricts. Coordinates belong to a finite stage, so the topology is exactly the inverse-limit topology. Compactness and finite-stage surjectivity prove rho:X_s->X=V_a(R) is continuous surjective, also at nonminimal supports. One can see surjectivity by the finite-intersection property for the nonempty compact finite-stage fibres.

Every rho-fibre is a FULL Gamma orbit. Indeed R_E^Gal(E/k)=R: expand in a k-basis of E and impose invariance, or use the trace-dual coefficient argument below. Its generic extension is Galois of degree [E:k] by geometric integrality and n2's fixed-field proof. Thus G331's full-support normal-target coefficient trace identifies each finite-stage fibre with a full Gal(E/k) orbit. Given w,w' in the same infinite fibre, let C_E be the set of gamma in Gamma for which their E-restrictions agree after gamma. Each C_E is nonempty clopen, because finite-field automorphisms extend to k^s and the fibre is an orbit. Finite intersections contain C_F for a common finite Galois F. The profinite compactness of Gamma gives a common gamma. This proves full transitivity, not merely transitivity on original-field valuations. Gamma is the inverse limit of the finite Galois groups; its compactness and restriction surjectivity are ordinary separable field theory, and the finite-intersection argument is supplied here.

Here is COMPLETE ideal descent, avoiding an infinite average. For finite Galois E/k choose a k-basis e_j and trace-dual c_i with Tr(c_i e_j)=delta_ij. Nondegeneracy can be proved without an extra theorem: n2's evaluation-matrix fixed-field proof gives a basis whose matrix M=(sigma(e_j)) is invertible. The trace Gram matrix is M^t M, with determinant (det M)^2 nonzero; its entries lie in k. Thus a trace-dual basis exists, also when the characteristic divides the group order. If an ideal I_E in R_E is Galois-stable and s=sum_j r_j e_j belongs to it, then sum_sigma sigma(c_i s)=r_i belongs to I_E intersect R. Hence I_E=(I_E intersect R)R_E.

If an ideal I_s in R_s is Gamma-stable, choose a finite Galois E containing its finite set of generators and let I_E be the generated ideal. R_s is faithfully flat over R_E (field extension), so I_s intersect R_E=I_E. Every automorphism of E extends to Gamma, and stability of I_s forces stability of I_E. Finite descent therefore gives I_s=(I_s intersect R)R_s. This proves the assertion on the entire Noetherian algebra, not just on a generic field. Primary and unit ideals retain their type: proper primary ideals contain a power of m_s=mR_s, and faithful contraction contains a power of m and remains proper.

For any finite continuous signed f on X, put F=f composed with rho. The source canonical B_m=A_m^(R_s)(F) is Gamma-stable by its all-support definition. Restriction surjectivity proves B_m intersect R=A_m^R(f). Ideal descent now gives the exact EVERY-degree identity

 B_m=A_m^R(f)R_s,  h_m^(R_s)=rho^*h_m^R,
 direct-sum B_m t^m=(direct-sum A_m^R t^m) tensor_k k^s.

Taking the raw supremum identity of n1 proves rho^*p_R(f)=p_(R_s)(F), WITHOUT first assuming either envelope continuous. Continuity of either raw envelope is equivalent to continuity of the other: pullback preserves continuity, and continuous fibre-constant functions descend through the compact quotient rho. The uniform criterion of n1 then proves positivity in C whenever continuous. Sup norms and all uniform canonical error bounds are preserved exactly, without a field-degree loss. Finite generation of the two canonical algebras is also equivalent: if the source is generated in degrees <=D, the multiplication maps from base degrees <=D become surjective after faithfully flat extension, hence were already surjective; finitely many generators of those Noetherian ideals suffice. The reverse is base extension. This is an equivalence, not general finite generation.

For completeness the positive continuous cone itself descends: rho^*C_R is precisely the Gamma-invariant subclass of C_(R_s). Pullback is an isometry and preserves C,D by primary ideal extension and actual limits. If H in source C is invariant, approximate it uniformly within epsilon by -w(I)/r. Descend its generators and primary-power containment to finite Galois E. Replace I_E by I'_E=sum_sigma sigma(I_E), whose profile is the maximum of its translates and is within epsilon of H on every source point, by Gamma invariance. I'_E is stable, unit or proper primary. The trace-dual proof descends it to J in R, giving the approximant -v(J)/r downstairs. Compact quotient descent and these uniform approximants put H in C_R. No assertion that arbitrary invariant D nets automatically descend through an infinite extension is needed or made.

Actual NEW CE application: in characteristic zero k^s is an algebraic closure. Let a finite group G act faithfully by k-linear transformations on k[x_1,...,x_n], preserving the origin, and take R=(k[x]^G) at its origin. The same result holds for any such geometrically normal rational germ whose algebraic-closure ring has the finite smooth-quotient presentation of n2. In the displayed linear case, invariants commute with field extension: the fixed-subspace equations on each finite-dimensional polynomial degree piece commute with tensoring, and localization commutes by invariant orbit denominator products. The invariant ring is finite type and k[x] finite over it: each variable satisfies its monic orbit polynomial, giving finiteness over the finite coefficient subalgebra; the invariant ring is its Noetherian submodule. All nonleading orbit-polynomial coefficients vanish at the origin, so modulo the invariant origin ideal every variable is nilpotent. Thus the origin is the unique centre above it, and the localized smooth cover is actually finite local. Normality follows from the integral invariant-fraction argument in n2, and the same argument after any field extension gives geometric normality and integrality. Thus R_s is the exact algebraically closed characteristic-zero finite smooth quotient of n2. That note applies BFJ ONLY there. Our independently proved full-fibre and ideal descent now gives a greatest continuous geometric C/D envelope for EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on R over ANY characteristic-zero field k.

For each signed REAL Cartier obstacle on an ACTUAL primary model, G331's section formula is a finite signed primary combination. Its scalar pullback is therefore a model obstacle in n2. The n2 quotient O(1/m) full-degree canonical estimate transfers EXACTLY to R through the every-degree identity above. The constant may depend on the geometric source model and obstacle; there is no field-extension-degree factor or finite-generation hypothesis. Exact primary-gauge changes leave all canonical ideals unchanged and divide errors by the positive gauge denominator.

In particular k=Q and R=Q[a,b,c,z_1,...,z_r]_(a,b,c,z)/(ac-b^2), r>=1, are actual normal nonisolated germs covered by the theorem. Normality, dimension r+2 and singular locus of dimension r follow from n2's explicit invariant presentation and derivative/embedding-dimension computation, which remain valid over characteristic-zero k. The same nonlinear signed primary obstacle and two cancellation-sensitive valuations in n2 exist over Q. Its continuous geometric envelope now follows over Q itself, rather than by applying a published algebraically closed theorem directly to Q. This supplies a complete new scoped theorem beyond whole410's stated base-field domain. It does not treat arbitrary normal singularities without the geometric smooth-quotient presentation, mixed characteristic, or provide a positive-characteristic CE source theorem. All normalization/conductor rules remain conditional on EVERY actual fibre; products and energy remain separate.

notes.detailedSummary: Proves explicit semivaluation homeomorphism, rational primary descent and isometric C/D equivalence, giving all-obstacle envelope commutation. Applies to finite purely inseparable extensions of normal domains and perfect closure of geometrically normal rational finite-type germs over imperfect fields; positive-characteristic CE remains conditional, mixed characteristic excluded.
notes.text:
NEW Frobenius-root invariance on the entire geometric envelope class. Let R subset S be an injective finite local extension of excellent reduced positive-dimensional rings of characteristic p>0. Assume a fixed q=p^e satisfies s^q in R for EVERY s in S. This hypothesis holds when R is a normal domain, S a finite domain, and Frac(S)/Frac(R) is finite purely inseparable: choose q killing that extension; s^q lies in Frac(R), is integral over R and hence lies in R. No perfection, F-finiteness, CM, Q-Gorenstein or resolution hypothesis is imposed. This is a proved envelope transport theorem; it supplies no unproved positive-characteristic regularity input.

Fix a primary ideal a in R. Restriction rho:V_(aS)(S)->V_a(R) is an actual homeomorphism with inverse

 w(s)=v(s^q)/q, including infinity/q=infinity.

The formula has w|R=v. Frobenius additivity (s+t)^q=s^q+t^q and multiplicativity prove the semivaluation axioms. Because aS is primary and w(aS)=1, the source maximal ideal has positive finite value. For example n^N subset mS subset n gives 0<w(m)/N<=w(n)<=w(m)<infinity. Supports are determined by s^q in supp(v), including nonminimal supports. Any lift must have this value by multiplicativity, so it is unique. Both maps are continuous by coordinate evaluations and scalar division, or by compact bijection. This proves full fibre compatibility rather than assuming generic inseparability controls every support.

The independently geometric classes C and D are isometrically identical under rho. One may invoke G331's full finite-injection positive descent since every fibre is singleton, but there is also an explicit ideal proof. If I=(s_1,...,s_l) is unit or proper primary in S, put J=(s_1^q,...,s_l^q) in R. Then v(J)=q w(I) on EVERY support. If I contains (aS)^N, raising any expression x=sum_i s_i u_i for x in a^N to the qth power shows x^q in J, since all u_i^q are in R. Thus J has radical m; it is proper when I is proper and is unit when I is unit. Hence the rational profile -w(I)/r is exactly the pullback of -v(J)/(qr). Primary ideal extension gives the reverse inclusion. Rational density and uniform closure identify C; actual decreasing C-nets identify D in both directions.
